Fixes #262

Claude Code gives a plugin SessionEnd hook 1.5s and ignores the `"timeout": 60` in hooks.json ("Timeouts set on plugin-provided hooks don't raise the budget"), then cancels it. The hook did its largest work first (a full claim-ledger scan, three git spawns, a 3s collector wait, a 10s telemetry finalize), so a cancel lost everything.

## Change
- **End note first.** `RecordSessionEndNote` appends one fsynced JSON line (`session_id`, `ended_at`, `reason`, `transcript_path`, plus `outcome`) to `.wipnote/sessions/<id>/session-end.ndjson` (gitignored). No subprocess, no shard scan. The cobra wrapper writes it before the DB opens.
- **Essential writes in the window.** Ledger row and claim episodes close with no `headCommit`. The claim root comes from the session id, `WIPNOTE_PARENT_SESSION` or the session family; there is no `ReadAll`.
- **Commit intents without git.** In the SessionEnd process, ledger commit intents are enqueued with no `rev-parse` or `check-ignore`; `commit-queue flush` does the git work.
- **Collector.** One SIGTERM, no wait, no SIGKILL.
- **Deferred to `CatchUpEndedSessions`** (idempotent, no detached process): end commit, handoff, lineage, features worked on, spike-worktree cleanup, collector drain/kill, telemetry finalize. It closes any open ledger row or episode with the note's end time and outcome (abandoned, not expired). `ReapStaleSessionsAndCollectors` runs it first: shallow on the session-start path, deep when `maxSessions <= 0` (the existing `config.go` caller). Exported for the daemon; the daemon files are untouched.
- Claim store removes `.claims-*.tmp` older than 5 minutes on the next write.
- Fixed the wrong "Claude Code grants 60s" comment, quoting the docs rule. No launcher env var; hooks.json keeps 60.
- Retention: `archiveSession` tars only `events.ndjson` and removes the session dir, so an uncaught-up note is dropped on archive. The shallow catch-up runs at every session start, long before the 30-day sweep.

## Tests (two-sided)
Window under a 25ms-per-op slow fs, 14 shards and a git stub that sleeps 500ms; a guard that fails on git or a claims scan before the note (and a subtest proving it catches the old ordering); a SIGTERM/SIGKILL cancel matrix on the real `hook session-end` in a child process at 0 to 1400ms; a SIGTERM-ignoring collector; catch-up idempotency and outcome; happy-path handoff after catch-up; stale temp removal.

## Timing (Linux, warm cache, copy of a real repo, wall ms, 10 runs each)
- Before: median ~340, range 212 to 1563.
- After: median ~250, range 230 to 2155 (one load outlier).
- Slow-fs test: SessionEnd ~183ms over 6 probed ops with 500ms git stubs, under the old design ~1s+ from git alone.
- The 0.9 to 1.4s cold figure was not reproduced on this warm machine. A macOS bind mount was not tested.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

unparsable lease younger than the window counts as held. Release checks
the owner token.

only while it is the inode this listener bound. A writer exits within one
watch interval once the lease or socket stops being its own, and after
5 minutes with no client even mid-hydrate; the hydrate stops between
passes on ctx. A live legacy writer.pid owner is left alone, and the
launcher prints one line for it or for an older-version owner.
